card.decision: Should `python src/cli.py TEXT N` remain a supported way to run the CLI, given that the sys.path insert at import time exists only for it?

experts.why: sys.path mutation at import time to support one invocation style

options.consequence: Importing src.cli has no side effects and the noqa goes away. Anyone running `python src/cli.py` must switch to the -m form.
options.label: Remove the sys.path insert; document `python -m src.cli TEXT N` as the run command.

options.consequence: `python src/cli.py` keeps working. Every importer of src.cli keeps the global path change, and the pattern is more likely to be copied.
options.label: Keep the sys.path insert as it is.

options.consequence: Imports are side-effect free, but the E402 workaround stays because the import of src.textstats still follows the insert in the file.
options.label: Keep direct-script support but move the insert under `if __name__ == "__main__":`.

ticket.purpose: Add `top_words(text, n)` to `src/textstats.py`. It returns the `n` most frequent words as `(word, count)` tuples, most frequent first. Reuse the existing `words` helper.
ticket.title: Add top_words to textstats

card.while_waiting: This ticket is parked at review; other tickets continue.
card.why: src/cli.py inserts the repo root into sys.path at module import, so every importer of src.cli gets a changed import path and the file needs a noqa: E402. Running `python -m src.cli TEXT N` from the repo root needs no path change. The same import-time pattern may be copied in the tests, which the plan requires to keep their sys.path bootstrap.
